title: Egusi Soup
subtitle: West African leafy green and spiced groundnut soup
excerpt: Egusi soup is a staple across much of West and Central Africa, traditionally made with ground melon seeds that thicken the soup and add a rich, earthy flavour. Peanut butter makes a practical substitute that closely approximates the texture and richness of the original. Spinach and a long-cooked tomato base give the soup its body.
sourceNotes: Egusi soup is found across West Africa from Nigeria and Ghana to Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of Congo, with each country and region having its own variation. The dish is one of the most significant in Nigerian cuisine, eaten at celebrations and everyday meals alike.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.

content.text: Cook the tomato base until very dry and the oil is clearly visible on the surface before adding the peanut butter. This concentrated base is what gives the soup its depth.

items.prepNote: 1 roughly chopped for blending, 1 finely diced for frying
smooth, used as a substitute for ground egusi melon seeds

content.text: Blend the tinned tomatoes, red pepper, chilli, and the roughly chopped onion until smooth. Set aside.
Heat the sunflower oil in the stockpot over medium-high heat. Add the finely diced onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Pour in the blended tomato mixture and add the coriander-ground. Cook, stirring frequently, for 15 minutes until the sauce has reduced and the oil begins to separate from the top.
Add the peanut butter and stir until it is fully incorporated into the sauce. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 20 minutes until the soup has thickened.
Add the spinach in batches, stirring each addition until wilted before adding the next. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt, then serve with fufu, pounded yam, or white rice.

items.cause: The peanut butter has been cooked for too long, or the stock has reduced too much
items.fix: Add hot water or more stock, a ladleful at a time, stirring well between additions until you reach the consistency you want.

items.cause: The tomato base was not cooked down long enough
items.fix: Egusi soup needs a properly reduced tomato base for depth. Next time, give step 3 the full 15 minutes. For now, simmer uncovered for longer to concentrate the flavours.
